title: MLCC Serve Engine Manifest
description: Per-engine serve-layer plugin manifest. Declares an engine's capabilities as data so do/draft, do/deploy, and .optimize_engine.py read engine knowledge from the manifest instead of hardcoded logic.

engine.description: Engine name; matches the plugin directory name (e.g. vllm, sglang).

env_var_prefix.description: Environment-variable prefix, e.g. VLLM_ or VLLM_OMNI_. Uppercase, with a trailing underscore; interior underscores are allowed for multi-token engine names (e.g. vLLM-Omni → VLLM_OMNI_).

speculative_decoding.description: Whether the engine supports speculative decoding at all. When false, supported_algorithms is [] and algorithm_map is {} — an explicit 'none' rather than an omitted field (ADR-004).

supported_algorithms.description: Speculative-decoding algorithms the engine actually supports. Empty [] when speculative_decoding is false.

algorithm_map.description: Maps MLCC algorithm names to engine-specific names.

hot_reload.description: Whether the engine supports hot reload.

min_version.description: Engine-agnostic capability versioning (BL129). Lowest engine version (semver) at which MLCC supports configuring this engine's version-gated capabilities. When the detected engine version is below this, consumers treat the engine as having no gated capabilities (fail-open — never blocks). Omit when the engine declares no minimum.

version_features.description: Engine-agnostic capability versioning (BL129). Version-gated capability additions: each entry's `adds` apply to the effective capability set ONLY when the detected engine version >= `since`. The flat fields (e.g. supported_algorithms) describe the engine's latest/default capabilities; version_features records when each of those landed, so a consumer resolving the effective set for an older version removes not-yet-available capabilities. An engine with no version-specific behavior omits this field (or []) — the effective set then equals the flat set for every version.

since.description: Engine version (semver) at and above which the `adds` capabilities are available.

adds.description: Capabilities that become available at `since`. Keys mirror the flat capability fields; a value must be a subset of the corresponding flat field.

supported_algorithms.description: Speculative-decoding algorithms that become available at `since`. Must be a subset of the flat supported_algorithms.

metrics_endpoint.description: Describes the engine's metrics endpoint (consumed by BL108).

dimension_map.description: Maps a benchmark dimension to an engine config key / flag suffix. Combined with env_var_prefix to yield the full config key.

engine_features.description: Engine-specific capabilities that are UNIQUE to this engine or implemented differently from the others (ADR-004 §c). Each entry is a named feature declared as DATA — its controlling env var, type, allowed values, and default — so a consumer reads it generically instead of branching on the engine name. This is the home for 'this engine can do X and vLLM cannot' (e.g. SGLang RadixAttention, LMI pluggable rolling-batch backend). Omit when the engine has no distinctive feature to declare. The feature KEY is an MLCC-stable snake_case name; the env_var is what the container actually reads.

env_var.description: The engine environment variable that controls this feature (what the container reads, e.g. SGLANG_ENABLE_RADIX_CACHE).

type.description: The value type the env var accepts. 'enum' requires `values`.

values.description: Allowed values. Required (and enforced via if/then) when type is 'enum'; omit otherwise.

default.description: The engine's default value when the env var is unset (string form, e.g. "false", "auto").

description.description: One line explaining what the feature does and how it differs from the other engines.

then.description: An 'enum' feature MUST declare its non-empty `values`; without them the feature would be unsettable (every value rejected).
